summary: Added tests for the agent-server linked extension loader and fixed it to support directory-based Pi extensions (with `index.ts` entry points) alongside legacy flat `.ts` files. Verified end-to-end by restarting the dev server, re-installing extensions via the registry protocol, and confirming project domain detection, web bundle emission, and pi symlink layout.
decisions: Linked Pi extensions can now be either a single `<id>.ts` file or a `<id>/` directory whose `index.ts` is loaded; symbolic links to directories are followed.

Test fixtures for linked directory extensions place the real source files in a separate temp dir and symlink the directory into the test root, so symlink-resolution paths remain distinct from real ones.

Each registry Pi extension exports a named `gizmoExtension = { id, name }` descriptor (added to activity and svelte) in addition to its default function, so the loader can pick up the metadata regardless of which entry shape is used.
`registry-manager` now directory-links the extension into `~/.pi/agent/extensions/<id>` (instead of copying a single `.ts`), and continues to manage the host-only web bundle as part of the same unit.
`docs/extensions.md` was updated to describe extensions as directory-linked into Pi, with `index.ts` entry points and sibling `<id>.web.js` bundles.
errors: First run of the new `loadLinkedExtensionIntegrations` test failed because the symlinked `source.ts` lived inside the same temp root, causing the loader to walk both the symlink and the real file and produce duplicate integration entries; fixed by moving the real source into a separate `sourceRoot` temp dir so only the directory symlink is seen by the loader.
